title: Patient-specific embryonic stem cells derived from human SCNT blastocysts
central_claims: Eleven patient-matched pluripotent embryonic stem-cell lines were produced from human SCNT blastocysts efficiently across patient sex and age.

source_manifest.title: SNU Investigation Committee: Summary of the Final Report on Professor Woo Suk Hwang’s Research Allegations
source_manifest.finding: The 2005 article claimed eleven lines; only two underlying lines existed and came from IVF, not SCNT. Fingerprinting, teratoma photographs, MHC matches and other evidence were fabricated. Report distinguishes some cloned-blastocyst technical ability from failure to establish the claimed patient-specific cell lines.

source_manifest.title: Tachibana et al. Human Embryonic Stem Cells Derived by Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer
source_manifest.finding: Read indexed author discussion and abstract: reports first successful human SCNT-derived embryonic stem cells through systematic protocol changes. This establishes later feasibility of the broader goal, not authenticity of Hwang’s reported eleven lines.

research.summary: The claimed eleven patient-specific stem-cell lines were not authentic SCNT products according to the primary investigation. Later successful human SCNT is a different achievement and does not validate this paper’s fabricated results.
